session: US open Fri 27 Nov, 22:30 SGT (half day, closes 13:00 ET; markets shut Thu 26 Nov for Thanksgiving)
bottom_line: Most ratings still hold, but only as small starter positions: the nine Overweight names are mostly below their rated prices and the overweight segments (cooling, grid, power) held up best again. Friday is a thin half-day after a correction, and Nvidia's SE Asia shipment halt is a named worldview risk, so size small and don't chase the open.
what_changed: US stocks are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving; Friday trades a half day to 13:00 ET (Newsweek, CME schedule).
Wednesday's close: S&P -0.2% and Nasdaq -0.6% after recovering from steeper intraday losses; VIX -4.2% to 27.1 (Yahoo live blog).
Nvidia halted AI server shipments to four SE Asian countries; Dell and Super Micro told buyers orders cannot ship. This hits the export-risk thesis directly.
Futures pointed higher into Black Friday before the holiday; no news dated after the Wednesday close turned up in searches.
Oracle bond yields hit 9% and Alphabet CDS at a record: the hyperscaler capex-credit risk is still building.

trust: Only 14 of 74 ratings are graded so far (grading starts after 28 days). Buy/Overweight picks average -5.9% vs QQQ: better than the no-AI screen (-20.0%) and random picks (-8.7%), but behind simply holding QQQ.
if_buying: Overweight means a small starter position, not full size; the track record so far does not beat QQQ.

Wait on MU until its 17 Dec earnings, and on AMAT and ANET while their segments are neutral.
